title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Aortic arch. Begins and ends at the sternal angle level; gives the brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian arteries.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Brachiocephalic veins. Formed by internal jugular + subclavian veins; the left crosses behind the manubrium to join the right and form the SVC.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Posterior structures. Oesophagus and thoracic duct, with the vagus nerves and left recurrent laryngeal nerve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Pulmonary trunk. From the conus arteriosus; divides at T5-T6 behind the 3rd left costal cartilage.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Superior vena cava. Formed behind the 1st right costal cartilage, enters the RA at the 3rd; receives the azygos vein.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Thymus. Behind the manubrium; large in children, atrophies after puberty; may contain ectopic parathyroids.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Trachea. Bifurcates at the sternal angle level.

title: Boundaries and contents of the superior mediastinum?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Boundaries and contents of the superior mediastinum?
body.back: Behind manubrium, in front of T1-T4, above the sternal angle-T4/T5 plane; thymus, brachiocephalic veins, SVC, aortic arch and branches, trachea, oesophagus, thoracic duct, phrenic and vagus nerves.

title: Pulmonary trunk?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Pulmonary trunk?
body.back: From the conus arteriosus; divides at T5-T6 into right (behind aorta and SVC) and left (below arch) pulmonary arteries.

title: Ascending aorta and aortic sinuses?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Ascending aorta and aortic sinuses?
body.back: From LV to 2nd right costal cartilage; three sinuses above the valve; coronary arteries from right and left sinuses.

title: Branches of the aortic arch?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Branches of the aortic arch?
body.back: Brachiocephalic trunk (R subclavian, R common carotid), left common carotid, left subclavian.

title: Formation of the SVC?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Formation of the SVC?
body.back: Right + left brachiocephalic veins behind the 1st right costal cartilage; enters RA at the 3rd; receives azygos.

title: The thymus?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: The thymus?
body.back: Most anterior in superior mediastinum; large in children, atrophies after puberty; ectopic parathyroid site.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Anterior compartment. Elbow and shoulder flexors, all supplied by the musculocutaneous nerve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Brachial canal. Medial space in front of the medial septum carrying the main neurovascular bundle.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Humerus. Central bone with the radial groove behind.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Posterior compartment. Triceps brachii (elbow extension) with the radial nerve and deep brachial artery in the radial groove.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Intermuscular septa. Separate the anterior and posterior compartments.

title: Compartments of the arm?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Compartments of the arm?
body.back: Anterior (biceps, brachialis, coracobrachialis; musculocutaneous n.) and posterior (triceps; radial n.), separated by the medial and lateral intermuscular septa.

title: Biceps brachii?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Biceps brachii?
body.back: Short head: coracoid. Long head: supraglenoid tubercle. → Radial tuberosity. Elbow flexion, supination.

title: Brachialis and coracobrachialis?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Brachialis and coracobrachialis?
body.back: Brachialis: humerus → coronoid; elbow flexion. Coracobrachialis: coracoid → medial humerus; arm flexion.

title: Triceps brachii?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Triceps brachii?
body.back: Long head (infraglenoid), lateral head (above radial groove), medial head (below) → olecranon; elbow extension; radial nerve.

title: Contents of the brachial canal?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Contents of the brachial canal?
body.back: Brachial artery, two brachial veins, median nerve, ulnar nerve.

title: Branches of the brachial artery?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Branches of the brachial artery?
body.back: Muscular, profunda brachii, superior and inferior ulnar collaterals; ends as radial and ulnar arteries.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Lateral group. Brachioradialis, extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Lateral bicipital groove. Radial nerve divides into a sensory branch and a motor branch that pierces supinator.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Medial group. From lateral to medial: pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Medial bicipital groove. Closed by the bicipital aponeurosis; brachial artery divides ~2 cm below the joint line; median nerve; site of the brachial pulse.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Median group. Biceps tendon to the radial tuberosity and brachialis to the ulna (coronoid).

title: Boundaries of the cubital fold?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Boundaries of the cubital fold?
body.back: Horizontal lines ~4 cm above and below the elbow joint line; vertical lines through the epicondyles.

title: Three muscle groups?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Three muscle groups?
body.back: Medial: PT, FCR, PL, FCU. Lateral: brachioradialis, ECRL, ECRB. Median: biceps and brachialis tendons.

title: Contents of the bicipital grooves?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Contents of the bicipital grooves?
body.back: Medial: brachial artery (+ 2 veins) and median nerve. Lateral: radial nerve.

title: Branches of the radial nerve at the elbow?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Branches of the radial nerve at the elbow?
body.back: Anterior sensory branch; posterior motor branch piercing supinator to supply posterior forearm muscles.

title: Clinical uses and risks?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Clinical uses and risks?
body.back: Brachial pulse; 'M' veins → cephalic and basilic for venepuncture; after trauma check brachial artery, median, radial, ulnar nerves.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Anterior compartment. Wrist and finger flexors and pronators; median and ulnar nerves; radial and ulnar arteries with venae comitantes.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Skeleton. Radius laterally, ulna medially, joined by the interosseous membrane.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Lateral compartment. Brachioradialis (elbow flexion) and radial wrist extensors, supplied by the radial nerve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Anterior layers. Four layers from superficial to deep, as listed in the lecture.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Posterior compartment. Superficial finger and wrist extensors and anconeus; deep thumb and index muscles; all supplied by the deep branch of the radial nerve.

title: Layers of the anterior forearm?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Layers of the anterior forearm?
body.back: 1: PT, FCR, PL, FCU. 2: FDS. 3: FPL, FDP. 4: supinator, pronator quadratus.

title: FDS vs FDP?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: FDS vs FDP?
body.back: FDS → middle phalanges (flexes PIP). FDP → distal phalanges (flexes DIP); median n. for 2-3, ulnar n. for 4-5.

title: Median nerve territory in the forearm?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Median nerve territory in the forearm?
body.back: All anterior muscles except FCU and the medial half of FDP.

title: Ulnar nerve in the forearm?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Ulnar nerve in the forearm?
body.back: From the epicondylo-olecranon groove, under FCU; supplies FCU and medial FDP.

title: Radial artery course?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Radial artery course?
body.back: Under brachioradialis, then in the pulse groove between FCR (medial) and brachioradialis (lateral) tendons.

title: Lateral compartment muscles?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Lateral compartment muscles?
body.back: Brachioradialis (elbow flexion), ECRL and ECRB (wrist extension); radial nerve.

title: Posterior compartment muscles?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Posterior compartment muscles?
body.back: Superficial: anconeus, extensor digitorum, EDM, ECU. Deep: APL, EPB, EPL, extensor indicis; deep radial nerve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Hypothenar compartment. Four little-finger muscles: palmaris brevis, abductor, flexor and opponens digiti minimi.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Median nerve. Thenar branch supplies abductor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis and the superficial head of flexor pollicis brevis.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Middle palmar compartment. Finger flexor tendons and the interossei arising from the metacarpals.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Thenar compartment. Four thumb muscles, superficial to deep: abductor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis, flexor pollicis brevis, adductor pollicis.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Ulnar nerve. All hypothenar muscles, adductor pollicis, deep head of flexor pollicis brevis and all interossei.

title: Three compartments of the palm?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Three compartments of the palm?
body.back: Thenar (thumb), hypothenar (little finger), middle (flexor tendons, interossei).

title: Thenar muscles and nerves?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Thenar muscles and nerves?
body.back: APB, opponens pollicis, FPB (superficial head: median; deep: ulnar), adductor pollicis (ulnar).

title: Hypothenar muscles and nerve?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Hypothenar muscles and nerve?
body.back: Palmaris brevis, abductor, flexor and opponens digiti minimi; all ulnar nerve.

title: Interossei actions?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Interossei actions?
body.back: Dorsal abduct (DAB), palmar adduct (PAD); deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Carpal tunnel. Carpal bones behind, flexor retinaculum in front; contains the finger flexor tendons and the median nerve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Deep palmar arch. Radial artery + ulnopalmar branch; lies behind the flexor tendons.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Guyon canal. Superficial to the flexor retinaculum on the medial side; transmits the ulnar nerve and artery.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Radial artery. Pulse groove between brachioradialis and FCR tendons, then through the anatomical snuffbox to the back and into the palm at the first web space.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Superficial palmar arch. Ulnar artery + radiopalmar branch; lies in front of the flexor tendons.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Ulnar artery. Runs lateral to the pisiform, anterior, with the ulnar nerve.

title: Course of the radial artery at the wrist?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Course of the radial artery at the wrist?
body.back: Pulse groove (between brachioradialis and FCR) → radiopalmar branch → anatomical snuffbox → dorsum → 1st web space → deep arch.

title: Palmar arches?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Palmar arches?
body.back: Superficial: ulnar artery + radiopalmar branch, in front of flexor tendons. Deep: radial artery + ulnopalmar branch, behind them.

title: Carpal tunnel?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Carpal tunnel?
body.back: Carpal bones (posterior), flexor retinaculum (anterior); contains finger flexor tendons and median nerve.

title: Median nerve in the hand?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Median nerve in the hand?
body.back: Thenar branch (APB, OP, superficial FPB); interdigital nerves spaces 1-3; sensation thumb to lateral half of ring finger.

title: Ulnar nerve in the hand?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Ulnar nerve in the hand?
body.back: Guyon's canal; deep branch: interossei, adductor pollicis, hypothenar; superficial: 4th space and 5th finger; sensation medial half ring + little finger.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Aorta. Receives oxygenated blood; the coronary arteries arise just above the aortic valve cusps.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Left atrium. Most of the base; receives four pulmonary veins; in contact with the oesophagus.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Left ventricle. Conical, thick-walled to generate systemic pressure; outflow through the aortic valve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Pulmonary trunk. Guarded by the pulmonary semilunar valve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Right atrium. Receives deoxygenated blood from both venae cavae and the coronary sinus; auricle with pectinate muscles.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Right ventricle. Most of the anterior surface; trabeculae carneae, papillary muscles, chordae tendineae, moderator band.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Valves. Tricuspid (RA→RV), pulmonary (RV→trunk), mitral (LA→LV), aortic (LV→aorta).

title: Layers of the heart?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Layers of the heart?
body.back: Epicardium (visceral pericardium), myocardium, endocardium.

title: Borders of the heart?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Borders of the heart?
body.back: Superior: auricles, great vessels. Inferior: RV. Left: LV and left auricle. Right: SVC, RA, IVC.

title: Cardiac sulci and contents?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Cardiac sulci and contents?
body.back: Coronary sulcus (RCA, LCA, circumflex, coronary sinus); anterior IV groove (LAD, great cardiac vein); posterior IV groove (PDA, middle cardiac vein).

title: Pericardium and sinuses?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Pericardium and sinuses?
body.back: Fibrous + serous parietal layers, visceral epicardium; transverse sinus behind aorta/pulmonary trunk; oblique sinus behind the heart.

title: Features of the right heart?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Features of the right heart?
body.back: RA: venae cavae, coronary sinus, pectinate muscles, tricuspid valve. RV: trabeculae, papillary muscles, chordae, moderator band, pulmonary valve.

title: Features of the left heart?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Features of the left heart?
body.back: LA: 4 pulmonary veins, base of heart, touches oesophagus, mitral valve. LV: conical, thickest wall, aortic valve.

title: Coronary arteries?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Coronary arteries?
body.back: LCA → LAD (anterior LV, apex, septum) + circumflex (posterolateral LV). RCA → RA, RV, SA and AV nodes, posterior descending artery.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Anteroposterior axis. Movements in the frontal plane: abduction and adduction, e.g. at the shoulder.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Frontal plane. Vertical, side to side: divides the body into front (anterior) and back (posterior).

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Left-right axis. Movements in the sagittal plane: flexion and extension.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Sagittal planes. Median (midsagittal) divides into equal right and left halves; parasagittal into unequal parts.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Transverse plane. Horizontal: divides into upper (superior) and lower (inferior) parts; CT and MRI axial slices.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Vertical axis. Movements in the transverse plane: rotation, e.g. turning the neck.

title: Define anatomy and its origin.
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Define anatomy and its origin.
body.back: Study of body structure (morphology); Greek anatome = cutting up; Latin equivalent: dissection.

title: Levels of structural organisation?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Levels of structural organisation?
body.back: Chemical, cellular, tissue, organ, organ system, organism.

title: Subdisciplines of anatomy?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Subdisciplines of anatomy?
body.back: Gross (surface, regional, systemic), microscopic (histology), developmental (embryology), pathological, radiographic.

title: Radiotransparent vs radiopaque?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Radiotransparent vs radiopaque?
body.back: Transparent: air, fat (X-rays pass). Opaque: bone, calcium stones, heavy metals (X-rays absorbed).

title: Anatomical position?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Anatomical position?
body.back: Erect, feet flat, toes and eyes forward, palms facing anteriorly, thumbs away from the body.

title: Clinical positions?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Clinical positions?
body.back: Supine (face up), prone (face down), right and left lateral recumbent.

title: Paired directional terms?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Paired directional terms?
body.back: Superior/inferior (cranial/caudal), medial/lateral, anterior/posterior (ventral/dorsal), superficial/deep, proximal/distal (limbs).

title: Three planes?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Three planes?
body.back: Sagittal (median, parasagittal), frontal/coronal, transverse/horizontal.

title: Three axes and their movements?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Three axes and their movements?
body.back: Left-right: flexion/extension. Anteroposterior: abduction/adduction. Vertical: rotation.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Left main bronchus. Divides into superior and inferior lobar bronchi.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Left lung. Two lobes separated by the oblique fissure; cardiac notch and lingula.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Right main bronchus. Divides into superior, middle and inferior lobar bronchi.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Right lung. Three lobes separated by oblique and horizontal fissures; shorter and wider (higher right dome).

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Further branching. Tertiary (segmental) bronchi, then bronchioles ending in alveolar sacs where gas exchange occurs.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Trachea. From the larynx to the bifurcation at the T4-T5 level (sternal angle).

title: Pulmonary vs bronchial circulation?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Pulmonary vs bronchial circulation?
body.back: Pulmonary: deoxygenated blood for gas exchange (RV → lungs → LA). Bronchial: oxygenated blood nourishing lung tissue.

title: Branching of the airways?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Branching of the airways?
body.back: Trachea → main bronchi (T4-T5) → lobar (R 3, L 2) → segmental → bronchioles → alveolar sacs.

title: Parts of the lung?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Parts of the lung?
body.back: Base, apex (above rib 1), costal and mediastinal surfaces, hilum, three borders.

title: Contents of the lung root?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Contents of the lung root?
body.back: Main bronchus, pulmonary artery, pulmonary veins, nerves, lymphatics, sleeved by pleura.

title: Right vs left lung?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Right vs left lung?
body.back: Right: 3 lobes, oblique and horizontal fissures, shorter and wider. Left: 2 lobes, oblique fissure, cardiac notch, lingula.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Triangular interval. Below teres major: the radial nerve passes into the posterior arm.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Long head of triceps. From the infraglenoid tubercle; divides the space into two.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Quadrangular (humerotricipital) space. Lateral to the long head of triceps: axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Teres major. Lower boundary; adducts and medially rotates the arm.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Teres minor. Upper boundary; lateral rotator; axillary nerve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Triangular (omo-tricipital) space. Medial to the long head of triceps: circumflex scapular artery.

title: Superficial muscles of the scapular region?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Superficial muscles of the scapular region?
body.back: Trapezius (CN XI; elevates shoulder, retracts scapula) and latissimus dorsi (thoracodorsal n.; adducts, medially rotates).

title: Rotator cuff muscles in this region?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Rotator cuff muscles in this region?
body.back: Supraspinatus (abduction), infraspinatus and teres minor (lateral rotation); subscapularis is anterior.

title: Teres major, rhomboids, levator scapulae?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Teres major, rhomboids, levator scapulae?
body.back: Teres major: adduction, medial rotation. Rhomboids: retract scapula (dorsal scapular n.). Levator scapulae: elevates scapula.

title: Quadrangular and triangular spaces?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Quadrangular and triangular spaces?
body.back: Quadrangular: axillary nerve + posterior circumflex humeral artery. Triangular: circumflex scapular artery. Triangular interval: radial nerve.

title: Deltoid?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Deltoid?
body.back: Clavicular, acromial and spinal parts → deltoid tuberosity; abduction; axillary nerve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Anterior wall. Superficial: pectoralis major (adduction, medial rotation). Deep: pectoralis minor and subclavius within the clavipectoral fascia.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Contents. Axillary artery (5 branches) with the vein medially, the cords of the brachial plexus, and lymph nodes draining the breast, chest wall and limb.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Lateral wall. Coracobrachialis (musculocutaneous nerve) and the short head of biceps.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Medial wall. Serratus anterior (first 8 ribs; long thoracic nerve): protracts the scapula.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Posterior wall. Subscapularis (medial rotation; subscapular nerve) and the tendon of teres major.

title: Boundaries and regions of the shoulder?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Boundaries and regions of the shoulder?
body.back: Clavicle above, lower border of pectoralis major below, midsternal line medially, lateral arm laterally; anterior (pectoral + deltoid) and posterior regions.

title: Walls of the axilla?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Walls of the axilla?
body.back: Anterior: pectoralis major, pectoralis minor, subclavius. Posterior: subscapularis, teres major. Medial: serratus anterior. Lateral: coracobrachialis, short head of biceps.

title: Pectoralis major?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Pectoralis major?
body.back: Clavicle, sternum, ribs 1-6, rectus sheath → lateral lip of bicipital groove; adduction and medial rotation; pectoral nerves.

title: Clavipectoral fascia?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Clavipectoral fascia?
body.back: Encloses subclavius and pectoralis minor; forms the suspensory ligament of the axilla; pierced by the cephalic vein and thoracoacromial artery.

title: Branches of the axillary artery?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Branches of the axillary artery?
body.back: Thoracoacromial, superior thoracic, subscapular, inferior thoracic, common trunk of circumflex humeral arteries.

title: Cords of the brachial plexus and their nerves?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Cords of the brachial plexus and their nerves?
body.back: Lateral: musculocutaneous, lateral root of median. Medial: medial root of median, ulnar, medial cutaneous nerves. Posterior: axillary, radial.

title: Drainage of axillary lymph nodes?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Drainage of axillary lymph nodes?
body.back: Breast, anterolateral chest wall, upper limb.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Elbow joint. Humero-ulnar (trochlea with trochlear notch), humeroradial (capitulum with radial head) and proximal radio-ulnar joints in one capsule with collateral ligaments.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Scapulohumeral joint. Humeral head and glenoid deepened by the labrum; lax capsule; coracohumeral and three glenohumeral ligaments in front; little bony interlocking, so dislocations (mostly anterior) are common.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Surface landmarks. The anatomical snuffbox is bounded by the extensor pollicis longus tendon medially and extensor pollicis brevis plus abductor pollicis longus laterally.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Radiocarpal joint. Distal radius and triangular fibrocartilage with scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum.

title: Five regions of the upper limb?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Five regions of the upper limb?
body.back: Shoulder, arm, elbow, forearm, hand.

title: Shoulder surface landmarks?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Shoulder surface landmarks?
body.back: Deltoid stump, lateral clavicle, acromioclavicular joint, deltopectoral groove (lost in dislocation), scapular spine and acromion, axilla.

title: Elbow surface anatomy?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Elbow surface anatomy?
body.back: Biceps and epicondylar masses, medial and lateral bicipital grooves, brachial pulse, 'M' veins; olecranon-epicondyle triangle in flexion, line in extension.

title: Wrist and hand landmarks?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Wrist and hand landmarks?
body.back: Radial pulse between FCR and brachioradialis; thenar and hypothenar eminences; creases; anatomical snuffbox (EPL medial, EPB + APL lateral).

title: Components of a synovial joint?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Components of a synovial joint?
body.back: Cartilage-covered surfaces, capsule and ligaments, synovium secreting synovial fluid, sometimes fibrocartilage.

title: Shoulder joint?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Shoulder joint?
body.back: Humeral head + glenoid with labrum; lax capsule; coracohumeral and glenohumeral ligaments; 3 degrees of freedom; frequent anterior dislocation.

title: Elbow joint?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Elbow joint?
body.back: Humero-ulnar, humeroradial, proximal radio-ulnar in one capsule; collateral ligaments; flexion-extension; participates in pronation-supination.

title: Wrist joint?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Wrist joint?
body.back: Radius + triangular fibrocartilage with scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum; flexion-extension and radial/ulnar deviation.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Aortic hiatus. T12, behind the median arcuate ligament: aorta, thoracic duct, azygos vein.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Caval opening. T8, in the central tendon, right of midline: inferior vena cava (and right phrenic branches).

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Oesophageal hiatus. T10, in the right crus: oesophagus with the vagal trunks.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Origins. Lumbar crura (right L1-L3, left L1-L2), inner surfaces of the lower six ribs, back of the xiphoid; all fibres converge on the central tendon.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Phrenic nerve. Motor to the diaphragm; sensory to its central part, pericardium and pleura. 'C3, 4, 5 keep the diaphragm alive'.

title: Anterior thoracic wall muscles?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Anterior thoracic wall muscles?
body.back: Pectoralis major (flex, adduct, medially rotate humerus), pectoralis minor (stabilises scapula), subclavius (depresses clavicle); accessory inspiratory muscles.

title: Layers of intercostal muscles and actions?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Layers of intercostal muscles and actions?
body.back: External (raise ribs, inspiration), internal (lower ribs, expiration), innermost; nerves and vessels between internal and innermost.

title: Origins of the diaphragm?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Origins of the diaphragm?
body.back: Lumbar crura (R L1-L3, L L1-L2), costal (lower 6 ribs), sternal (xiphoid) → central tendon.

title: Innervation of the diaphragm?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Innervation of the diaphragm?
body.back: Phrenic nerves C3-C5: motor, and sensory to central diaphragm, pericardium, pleura.

title: Diaphragmatic openings?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Diaphragmatic openings?
body.back: Caval T8 (IVC), oesophageal T10 (oesophagus, vagal trunks), aortic T12 (aorta, thoracic duct).

title: Course of the phrenic nerve?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Course of the phrenic nerve?
body.back: On anterior scalene, between subclavian vein and artery, in front of lung root between mediastinal pleura and pericardium, to the diaphragm.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Intercostal artery. Between vein and nerve.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Intercostal nerve. Lowest, often below the groove, so most at risk when the upper part of a space is perforated.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Costal groove. Along the lower border of each rib, between the inner two intercostal muscle layers.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Clinical rule. Chest drains and needles pass just above the upper border of the rib below to avoid the bundle.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Rib classes. True ribs join the sternum directly; false ribs indirectly or not at all; floating ribs have no anterior attachment.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Intercostal vein. Most superior structure in the groove.

title: Components of the thoracic skeleton?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Components of the thoracic skeleton?
body.back: 12 thoracic vertebrae, 12 pairs of ribs, sternum and costal cartilages.

title: Parts of the sternum and levels?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Parts of the sternum and levels?
body.back: Manubrium (jugular notch, rib 1), body (cartilages 2-7), xiphoid (T9); sternal angle at T4-T5.

title: Clinical importance of the sternal angle?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Clinical importance of the sternal angle?
body.back: Rib 2 (count ribs), T4-T5 plane, start and end of aortic arch, tracheal bifurcation.

title: Classification of ribs?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Classification of ribs?
body.back: True 1-7 (direct), false 8-10 (via cartilage above), floating 11-12 (no anterior attachment).

title: Parts of a typical rib?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Parts of a typical rib?
body.back: Head, neck, tubercle, shaft with costal groove; ribs 2-10.

title: Atypical ribs?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Atypical ribs?
body.back: Rib 1 (scalene tubercle, subclavian vein groove in front and artery behind), ribs 11-12 (floating).

title: Intercostal neurovascular bundle?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Intercostal neurovascular bundle?
body.back: In the costal groove of the rib above: vein, artery, nerve (VAN), nerve least protected.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Anterior mediastinum. Between the sternum and the pericardium.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Middle mediastinum. The pericardium and the heart.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Transverse thoracic plane. Sternal angle (rib 2) to the T4-T5 intervertebral disc.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Posterior mediastinum. Between the pericardium and the thoracic vertebrae.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Superior mediastinum. Above the plane through the sternal angle and the T4-T5 disc.

title: Compartments of the thoracic cavity?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Compartments of the thoracic cavity?
body.back: Right and left pleural cavities (each with a lung) and the mediastinum between them.

title: Key surface landmarks?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Key surface landmarks?
body.back: Clavicles, jugular notch, sternal angle (rib 2, T4-T5); midsternal, midclavicular, anterior/mid/posterior axillary lines.

title: Superior thoracic aperture?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Superior thoracic aperture?
body.back: T1 body, medial margins of first ribs, manubrium; open to the neck.

title: Inferior thoracic aperture?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Inferior thoracic aperture?
body.back: T12, rib 12 and end of rib 11, costal cartilages 7-10, xiphoid; closed by the diaphragm.

title: Diaphragm key facts?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Diaphragm key facts?
body.back: Radial fibres to a central tendon; right dome higher (rib 5); oesophagus and IVC pierce it, aorta passes behind.

title: Subdivisions of the mediastinum?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Subdivisions of the mediastinum?
body.back: Superior (above sternal angle plane) and inferior: anterior, middle (heart, pericardium), posterior.

title: Pleura and recesses?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Pleura and recesses?
body.back: Parietal pleura on walls, visceral on lung, potential space between; costodiaphragmatic recess largest.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Anastomoses. Anterior and posterior intercostal arteries join in each space, a collateral route.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Anterior intercostal arteries. From the internal thoracic (upper spaces) and musculophrenic (7th-9th spaces) arteries.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Thoracic aorta. Gives posterior intercostal arteries 3-11 and the subcostal artery.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Internal thoracic artery. Runs inside the cage just lateral to the sternum; ends as musculophrenic and superior epigastric arteries.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Posterior intercostal arteries. Run forward between internal and innermost muscles.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Subclavian artery. Gives the internal thoracic artery and, via the costocervical trunk, the supreme intercostal artery.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Supreme intercostal artery. From the costocervical trunk; gives the first two posterior intercostal arteries.

title: Intercostal neurovascular bundle?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Intercostal neurovascular bundle?
body.back: Costal groove, between internal and innermost intercostals; vein, artery, nerve (VAN); nerves = ventral rami T1-T11.

title: Anterior arterial supply of the wall?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Anterior arterial supply of the wall?
body.back: Internal thoracic artery (subclavian) → anterior intercostals, perforators (medial mammary branches); ends as musculophrenic + superior epigastric.

title: Posterior arterial supply?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Posterior arterial supply?
body.back: Supreme intercostal artery (spaces 1-2) and thoracic aorta (posterior intercostals 3-11, subcostal).

title: Venous drainage of the wall?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Venous drainage of the wall?
body.back: Internal thoracic and anterior intercostal veins → brachiocephalic; posterior intercostal: upper two → brachiocephalic, lower nine → azygos → SVC.

title: Thoracic lymph nodes?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Thoracic lymph nodes?
body.back: Parasternal (medial breast, diaphragm), intercostal (→ thoracic duct), phrenic (→ mediastinal nodes).

title: Anatomy of the breast?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Anatomy of the breast?
body.back: Mammary gland over ribs 2-6, sternum to midaxillary line, in superficial fascia on pectoralis major and serratus anterior; retromammary space; lymph to axillary and parasternal nodes.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Arm. One long bone, the humerus.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Clavicle. Long S-shaped bone; pectoralis major and deltoid on the anterior border, sternocleidomastoid and trapezius on the posterior border.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Forearm. Radius laterally and ulna medially, joined by radio-ulnar joints and the interosseous membrane.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Hand. Carpus (8 bones), metacarpus (5), phalanges (14).

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Humerus. Head, greater and lesser tubercles, bicipital groove, deltoid tuberosity, radial groove (radial nerve), capitulum and trochlea, epicondyles.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Scapula. Flat triangular bone: subscapular fossa in front, spine dividing supra- and infraspinous fossae behind; glenoid cavity for the humeral head.

title: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: What is at the arrow, and why does it matter?
body.back: Pectoral girdle. Connects the thorax to the upper limb.

title: Segments of the upper limb?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Segments of the upper limb?
body.back: Shoulder, arm, forearm, hand.

title: Clavicle muscle insertions?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Clavicle muscle insertions?
body.back: Anterior border: pectoralis major (medial 2/3), deltoid (lateral 1/3). Posterior border: SCM (medial), trapezius (lateral). Inferior: subclavius.

title: Main features of the scapula?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Main features of the scapula?
body.back: Subscapular fossa, spine with supra- and infraspinous fossae, acromion, coracoid process, glenoid cavity, supra- and infraglenoid tubercles.

title: Coracoid process attachments?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Coracoid process attachments?
body.back: Pectoralis minor, coracobrachialis, short head of biceps.

title: Humeral tubercles?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Humeral tubercles?
body.back: Greater: supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor. Lesser: subscapularis. Between: bicipital groove (long head of biceps).

title: Distal humerus?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Distal humerus?
body.back: Capitulum (radius), trochlea (ulna), lateral epicondyle (extensors), medial epicondyle (flexors), olecranon fossa.

title: Radius landmarks?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Radius landmarks?
body.back: Head, neck, radial tuberosity (biceps), radial styloid (brachioradialis), ulnar notch; distal surface articulates with scaphoid and lunate.

title: Bones of the hand?
subject: subj:anat1

body.front: Bones of the hand?
body.back: 8 carpals (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform; trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate), 5 metacarpals, 14 phalanges.
